blocks.text:
Arrive in Lima, where you will be met and transferred to your hotel. Peru's capital stands on the Pacific coast. Spanish architecture sits alongside pre-Inca monuments, and the historic centre of old Lima is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

The tour begins at the Santo Domingo Convent, built during the city's founding period. The Universidad Mayor de San Marcos, the oldest university in the Americas, was founded here. The convent retains its historic choir stalls, and its library holds around 25,000 books, including editions from the 15th century. The remains of Saint Martin de Porres, Saint John Macias and Saint Rose of Lima also rest here.

Continue through Plaza Mayor, past the Government Palace and City Hall, to the Cathedral. Inside are works of colonial art. After exploring the historic centre, visit the Larco Museum. Its collection introduces the cultures of ancient Peru through gold objects, textiles and its famous collection of erotic pottery. The displays reveal how ancient Peruvians understood the world and connected everyday life with religious imagery.

In the evening, enjoy a romantic dinner at Casa Moreyra, the restaurant of renowned chef Gastón Acurio. It occupies the old manor house of the San Isidro estate. Gastón Acurio helped bring Peruvian cuisine to international attention.

blocks.text:
Arrive in Cusco and transfer to your hotel. In the afternoon, begin a walking tour of the city. Take in the panorama of Cusco from Plaza San Cristóbal, then visit San Pedro Market to see local produce and sample flavours familiar to the city's residents.

The next stop is Qorikancha. Its walls were once covered in gold, and the temple remains one of the key places to discover Cusco's Inca past. Continue through San Blas, the artisans' quarter, and along Hatun Rumiyoc street. Along the way stands the Inca Roca Palace, now the Archbishop's Palace, and nearby is the famous Twelve-Angled Stone, fitted to the surrounding blocks without mortar. The day ends at Plaza de Armas with a visit to the Cathedral and its valuable works of colonial art.
